strings.name: Shafi Goldwasser
strings.summary: Moving from mathematics into computing, Goldwasser worked with Silvio Micali and others on probabilistic encryption, zero-knowledge proofs and verifiable computation, giving security rigorous mathematical definitions. She researched at MIT, Weizmann and Berkeley and directed the Simons Institute. She and Micali received the 2012 Turing Award in 2013; her recent work addresses privacy and trustworthy machine learning.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; reviewed November 15, 2026. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced probabilistic encryption and zero-knowledge proofs, laying theoretical foundations for modern cryptography, secure computation and privacy protection.

strings.facts.f1.value: New York City, United States; authoritative sources give 1958 or 1959 as her birth year.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Carnegie Mellon bachelor’s (1979); UC Berkeley computer-science doctorate (1984).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Probabilistic encryption
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Micali and others, established rigorous definitions and provable-security methods.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Zero-knowledge proofs
strings.highlights.h2.text: With Micali and Charles Rackoff, developed proofs revealing no additional knowledge.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Directorship ended
strings.timeline.t1.text: Completed the 2018–2024 Simons directorship and continued research.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Simons director

strings.timeline.t5.title: Zero-knowledge proofs
strings.timeline.t5.text: Published the zero-knowledge idea for interactive proofs with collaborators.

strings.timeline.t9.title: Joined MIT
strings.timeline.t9.text: Joined MIT before completing her doctorate, beginning a long research career.
